new.n: O. M. Holcomb's 1857 gold working, west bank of the Iowa River, sec. 29 T88N R19W
new.pl: Sec. 29 T88N R19W (BLM PLSS), on the west bank of the Iowa River; quarter not given.
new.st: 1911 Hardin County history: 'In 1857 gold was discovered on section 29, on the west bank of the Iowa, being worked by O. M. Holcomb and others, he being an old gold miner of California.' It is the first named working on the Iowa River here. Pin: Sec. 29 T88N R19W (BLM PLSS), on the west bank of the Iowa River; quarter not given.
new.t: The river crosses sec. 29 just west of Steamboat Rock. Pan the west-bank gravels and any old cut bank. Private land; ask first. Access: Iowa Code 461A.35: no removing sand, gravel, earth or stone from state parks, preserves, meandered streams or other DNR commission lands except on commission terms; metal detectors limited by 571 IAC 64. Private banks and fields need the owner's OK.

new.n: Basal Mt. Simon conglomerate gold, Neillsville-Granton
new.st: WGNHS lists gold in the basal Mount Simon conglomerate around Neillsville and Granton in Clark County. This is the gravel at the bottom of the Cambrian sandstone, lying right on the old Precambrian bedrock. Pin: Region-level between Neillsville and Granton.

set.pl: Sec. 21 T37N R15W (BLM PLSS). WGNHS files it under Barron (Cumberland), but the section is in the town of Lorain, Polk County.
set.st: Oct 1905: Chas. Eckerts claimed gold nuggets on his farm in the town of Lorain, with 'pay dirt' said to be worth $2,000 a ton (Glenwood Tribune, via River Falls Journal). The WGNHS gold list independently records 1905 'Cumberland' nuggets in sec. 21 T37N R15W, the same place and year, so this is two sources. Pin: Sec. 21 T37N R15W (BLM PLSS). WGNHS files it under Barron (Cumberland), but the section is in the town of Lorain, Polk County.
set.t: Find Eckerts (or Eckert) in sec. 21 on the 1914-15 Polk County plat and look for creek gravel on that land. Treat the $2,000 a ton as boom talk. Access: Wisconsin: recreational panning with pans, screens, shovels, small manual sluices and metal detectors needs no DNR permit; no more than 2 cubic yards a year per waterway; no panning in State Parks, State Trails, State Recreation Areas, State Wild and Scenic Rivers, State Natural Areas or state-owned lakebeds (WI DNR Gold Panning page). Streambed to the center belongs to the riparian owner, and reaching the stream across private land needs the owner's OK.

set.n: Brunsweiler Creek gold claims, secs. 15 and 23 T45N R4W (1880)
set.pl: Sec. 23 T45N R4W (BLM PLSS), next to WGNHS's 'Brunschweiler Creek placer sec 22'. The 1880 paper says R. 3 W; WGNHS and the river's course say R. 4 W. The R3W sections 15/23 would be about 9 km east (46.371,-90.716), so a plat check is still wanted.
set.st: Spring 1880: gold 'discovered on Brunsweiler's creek some 12 or 15 miles south of Ashland. Quite a number of people are on the ground and claim shanties are being erected. So far the best find has been on sections 15 and 23, T. 45, R. 3 west' (Superior Times; numbers read from the page image). WGNHS lists a Brunschweiler Creek placer in sec. 22 T45N R4W, beside the Chicago Mine (1879-81, N½ sec. 22) and the Northern Belle (W½ SW sec. 22). Pin: Sec. 23 T45N R4W (BLM PLSS), next to WGNHS's 'Brunschweiler Creek placer sec 22'. The 1880 paper says R. 3 W; WGNHS and the river's course say R. 4 W. The R3W sections 15/23 would be about 9 km east (46.371,-90.716), so a plat check is still wanted.
set.t: This is the same square mile as the existing Chicago Mine target (g-PG) and a mile from the Chief Namakagon homestead (sec. 26). Pan the creek gravels in secs. 22-23 and look for claim-shanty pits on LiDAR. Check national forest ownership first. Access: Wisconsin: recreational panning with pans, screens, shovels, small manual sluices and metal detectors needs no DNR permit; no more than 2 cubic yards a year per waterway; no panning in State Parks, State Trails, State Recreation Areas, State Wild and Scenic Rivers, State Natural Areas or state-owned lakebeds (WI DNR Gold Panning page). May be inside Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest: historic sites there are look-only; check the district office before panning.
